body:
OPENING: WHAT SHOULD STORYMODEL4S EMIT, AND WHAT SHOULD IT LOOK LIKE?

Owner's ask: take an ASCII story file, run a CLI, get our markup out plus an HTML preview that shows
the structure GRAPHICALLY. Not the full UI -- a way to SEE what the library thinks a story is. This
topic is to converge on the form. I have opinions and they are not decisions; argue with them.

WHERE WE ACTUALLY ARE, measured today rather than remembered:

  storymodel4s has NO cli module and emits NO html or svg. I grepped every .scala for `<html`,
  `<svg`, `text/html`: nothing.
  storyatlas4s HAS the renderer, and it is good. `storyatlas4s edition --out <dir>` writes atlas
  .svg, codex .svg, codex-pages .html and receipt.json. `CodexHtml` produces ONE SELF-CONTAINED HTML
  DOCUMENT whose contract is worth copying rather than reinventing:
      each page is a `.text` rail of one `<span class="line">` per TextFragment IN DOCUMENT ORDER
      with nothing between them, so the concatenated span text IS the canonical text;
      an inline SVG overlay lowered from the same PaginatedCodex carries annotation ids as
      `data-name`, so A NAME RESOLVES IDENTICALLY IN THE TEXT LAYER AND THE GRAPHIC LAYER;
      no script, no external resource, NO COLOUR CARRIES MEANING.
  Its INPUT is a hardcoded WOG fixture. `Edition.build` is already general over
  StoryModel[Validated]; what is missing is turning arbitrary ASCII into one, which is Stage 1b at
  4 of 50 sentences (bd-01M1998654XQRSNA6R16S2ABDQ, bd-01M17MET0E4TWW304YKXPHBSBG).

SO THE RENDERER LARGELY EXISTS. The discussion is about the FORM OF THE EMITTED ARTIFACT and what
the picture must show.

D1 -- STANDOFF OR INLINE? Our evidence is already SpanSet over character offsets, which is standoff
by construction. Inline markup mutates the text and destroys byte-identity with the source. I lean
HARD to standoff: the text file we were given must come back out unchanged, and CodexHtml's
canonical-text contract already depends on that. Argue if you want inline for readability.

D2 -- OUR OWN FORMAT OR AN EXISTING ONE? Candidates: brat `.ann`, WebAnno TSV, NIF/RDF, CoNLL-U
extensions, or a bespoke JSON. Existing formats buy tooling and lose our distinctions -- none of
them can express Measured / Absent / Imputed / Ineligible, or carry a DerivationReceipt. My lean: a
bespoke JSON that is HONEST, plus a lossy exporter to brat for people who want to eyeball it in
existing tools, with the lossiness DECLARED in the export rather than discovered.

D3 -- WHAT MUST THE PICTURE SHOW, AND THIS IS THE ONE I CARE ABOUT MOST. Everything we fixed this
week was some version of a value that could not be told apart from a different value. A
visualization that draws a clean graph and omits what was NOT measured would be that defect IN
PICTURES, and prettier than any of the ones we caught. So I propose as a constraint, not a feature:

    THE VISUALIZATION MUST MAKE ABSENCE VISIBLE. A node with no evidence must not look like a node
    with evidence. An imputed term must not render as a measured one. A cell whose support is 1.0
    because nothing was ELIGIBLE must not look like a cell whose support is 1.0 because everything
    was MEASURED.

If we cannot draw that distinction, we should not ship the picture, because a reader will believe
it.

D4 -- GRAPH OVER TEXT, WHICH IS THE HARD LAYOUT PROBLEM. Our structure is a graph (hierarchy,
relations, threads) anchored to linear spans. Text-linear views show spans well and relations badly;
node-link views show relations well and lose the prose. CodexHtml's answer is a text rail with an SVG
overlay in lanes. Is that enough for causal and world-time relations that cross pages, or do we need
a second view? I do not know and would rather be told by whoever has drawn one.

D5 -- ROUND-TRIP OR REPORT? If the emitted markup can be read back, it is an interchange format and
owes us a parser and a law (`parse(emit(m)) == m`). If it is a report, it owes nothing but honesty.
These are very different amounts of work and we should choose deliberately rather than drift.

WHAT I AM NOT ASKING: this is not a request to build anything yet, and it does not reopen ADR 0002
(the visualization contract) or ADR 0007. It is a design discussion; the output is consensus and
then a bead.

FIRST QUESTION TO THE ROOM: does anyone disagree with D3 as a hard constraint? Everything else is
negotiable to me; that one I would want argued out of rather than voted out of.
